title: Naturality of the derived-composite isomorphism in the exact functor
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ with enough injectives, and $U:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ left exact [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Let $T,T':\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be exact functors such that $T(I)$ and $T'(I)$ are $U$-acyclic [def-sp-acyclic] for every injective $I$ of $\mathcal A$, and let $\alpha:T\to T'$ be a natural transformation. For an object $M$ of $\mathcal A$ with injective resolution $M\to I^\bullet$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], let $R^i(U\alpha)_M:R^i(U\circ T)(M)\to R^i(U\circ T')(M)$ be the map $\mathcal H^i(U(\alpha_{I^\bullet}))$. Since $T$ and $T'$ are exact, $T(M)\to T(I^\bullet)$ and $T'(M)\to T'(I^\bullet)$ are resolutions by $U$-acyclic objects; let $c_T^i:R^i(U\circ T)(M)=\mathcal H^i(U(T(I^\bullet)))\xrightarrow{\sim}R^iU(T(M))$ and $c_{T'}^i:R^i(U\circ T')(M)=\mathcal H^i(U(T'(I^\bullet)))\xrightarrow{\sim}R^iU(T'(M))$ be the comparison isomorphisms of item 2 of [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity] for these resolutions (the canonical isomorphisms of [lem-sc-ext-derived-composite]). Then for every $i\geq0$ one has $c_{T'}^i\circ R^i(U\alpha)_M=R^iU(\alpha_M)\circ c_T^i$.

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma Tag 015E (derived-lemma-leray-acyclicity, line 5717): the canonical map $F(A^\bullet)\to RF(A^\bullet)$ for a bounded below complex of $F$-acyclics, natural in $A^\bullet$; applied to the map of acyclic resolutions $\alpha_{I^\bullet}:T(I^\bullet)\to T'(I^\bullet)$ lifting $\alpha_M$

proof.text: Choose an injective resolution $M\to I^\bullet$ in $\mathcal A$. Exactness of $T$ and $T'$ carries it to exact bounded-below resolutions $T(M)\to T(I^\bullet)$ and $T'(M)\to T'(I^\bullet)$, and the components of $\alpha$ give a morphism over $\alpha_M$. By the hypotheses, every term is $U$-acyclic.

source.place: Lemma Tag 015M, proof: choose an injective resolution and apply the exact first functor

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-acyclic-comparison-natural] with $v=U$ (on $\mathcal B$, which has enough injectives), $F=T(M)$, $F'=T'(M)$, the $U$-acyclic resolutions $r:T(M)\to T(I^\bullet)$ and $r':T'(M)\to T'(I^\bullet)$ of Step 1, $h=\alpha_M$ and $\varphi=\alpha_{I^\bullet}$; the hypothesis $\varphi^0\circ r=r'\circ h$ is the naturality square of $\alpha$ for the augmentation $M\to I^0$. Its comparison isomorphisms are the maps $c_T^i,c_{T'}^i$ of the statement (both are the comparison isomorphisms of item 2 of [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity] for these resolutions), and its conclusion $c_{T'}^i\circ\mathcal H^i(U(\alpha_{I^\bullet}))=R^iU(\alpha_M)\circ c_T^i$ is the claim, since $R^i(U\alpha)_M=\mathcal H^i(U(\alpha_{I^\bullet}))$ by definition.

lean.statement: theorem rightDerived_exact_comp_iso_naturality {A : Type u₁} {B : Type u₂} {C : Type u₃} [Category.{v₁} A] [Category.{v₂} B] [Category.{v₃} C] [Abelian A] [Abelian B] [Abelian C] [EnoughInjectives A] [EnoughInjectives B] (T T' : A ⥤ B) (U : B ⥤ C) [T.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits T] [PreservesFiniteColimits T] [T'.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits T'] [PreservesFiniteColimits T'] [U.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits U] (hTU : ∀ (J : A), Injective J → U.rightAcyclic (T.obj J)) (hT'U : ∀ (J : A), Injective J → U.rightAcyclic (T'.obj J)) (α : T ⟶ T') (M : A) (I : InjectiveResolution M) (i : ℕ) : let cT := Classical.choose (exists_rightDerived_exact_comp_iso T U hTU M i) let cT' := Classical.choose (exists_rightDerived_exact_comp_iso T' U hT'U M i) (I.isoRightDerivedObj (T ⋙ U) i).hom ≫ HomologicalComplex.homologyMap ((NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex (whiskerRight α U) (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).app I.cocomplex) i ≫ (I.isoRightDerivedObj (T' ⋙ U) i).inv ≫ cT'.hom = cT.hom ≫ (U.rightDerived i).map (α.app M)
